# Temple Run APK - obstacle mesh assets

Original obstacle geometry extracted from the shipped APK (`com.imangi.templerun` 1.39.0, Unity 2022.3.62f2), converted to game-ready OBJ so the web port can stop drawing obstacles from procedural primitives.

* generated by `/tmp/export_temple_obstacles.py` (export) + `/tmp/verify_obstacles.py` (parse-back + obstruction raycast); re-run both to reproduce
* data: `analysis/obstacle-manifest.json` (authoritative: source prefab/mesh per file, measured bbox, texture, lane obstruction)
* visual proof / inspection page: `web/obstacle-tools/obj-sheet.html` - renders the actual exported OBJ files over the road plane with a player-height reference box, e.g. `?cols=2&rows=2&view=iso&files=tree-jump-left.obj,tree-slide.obj,pit.obj,flame-tower.obj`

## TL;DR

* **All five obstacle archetypes of the game exist as real shipped meshes** - and the prefab names even name the intended input: `treeJump*`, `treeTrip*`, `treeSlide*`, `flameTowerHigh*`, `StraightHole*`. They are *track-tile prefabs*, i.e. the obstacle mesh ships together with the wall tile it belongs to.
* **23 OBJ files, 1.0 MB total, exported + verified.** No texture was duplicated (both atlases already ship with the web game at `/assets/apk/`).
* **The road plane is the prefab-root y = 0.** The track tiles carry a ~30 u skirt *below* it (that is why exported track walls look 36.8 u tall instead of the ~6.8 u ruin wall you actually see in game). All OBJs here keep y = 0 = road surface, so dropping one at the road height puts it exactly right; the skirt disappears under the road.
* **No dedicated "small prop" obstacle exists**: no crate, barrel, spike trap, broken column, or brazier-with-flame mesh. The only low meshes in the whole APK are the 3 coin meshes (3.6 u). The flame of the flame tower is a ParticleSystem - no flame mesh and no flame texture exist, so fire has to stay procedural.

| Unity data | `/tmp/temple-unity-all/assets/bin/Data` (457 loadable serialized files) |

| method | (1) map every MeshRenderer -> prefab root chain, keyed by (file, path_id) because path ids are not unique across bundles; (2) read the prefab-root-relative transform of each mesh; (3) bake to the road frame; (4) raycast the baked mesh to measure what a runner would hit |

### How the obstacles were identified

The mesh *names* are useless (`Object105-Pivot`), but the **prefab/bundle names are the gameplay table of contents**. Every obstacle is a complete track-tile prefab of the form `templeStraight<Obstacle><Direction><Axis>_prefab`, and the mesh inside it is the obstacle:

```
templeStraightTreeJumpUpHorz_prefab      jump obstacle (fallen root across the path)
templeStraightTreeTripUpHorz_prefab      low trip root
templeStraightTreeSlideHorz_prefab       leaning trunk you slide under
templeStraightFlameTowerHighHorz_prefab  twin flame pedestals
templeStraightHoleHorz_prefab            pit / gap
templeStraightTowerHorz_prefab           tall run-through tower
templeStraightNarrowLongUpHorz_prefab    narrowing / low side wall
plankStraightTowerHorz_prefab            same archetypes on the wooden "plank" track section
```

Tree obstacles are two meshes: the wallTexture tile (already part of the track dressing) plus the treeTexture tree. Only the **obstacle mesh** is exported for those, because the tile is already covered by the exported track pieces; the single-mesh obstacles (flame tower, pit, tower, narrow wall) are exported whole.

## The one measurement that matters: the road plane

Naively the meshes look like they stand on their bounding-box bottom, which is 30 u below their authored origin. That is wrong, and everything about placement depends on getting it right:

| evidence | value |
|---|---|
| plain wall tile, authored | y = -30.0 ... +6.78, so a 6.78 u wall standing on a 30 u skirt |
| pit tile | y = -30.0 ... +2.72 -> a 30 u deep shaft with a 2.7 u rim above the floor |
| flame tower | y = -3.2 ... +14.9 -> a 15 u pedestal, not a 45 u tower |
| tree jump | the root mass occupies y = 0 ... 10 -> a jumpable waist-high root |
| tree slide | the trunk is open below y = 11, the runner is 10.8 u tall -> a duck-under |

Only with the road at prefab y = 0 do these read as the objects the game actually asks the player to react to (jump / slide / gap / run between flames). The 30 u below is the authored ground skirt that the original game hides under its procedural road.

**Consequence for the track pieces that are already in the web game**: they were exported with `minY = 0`, so they include the skirt. Placed at road height they show 36.8 u walls instead of 6.78 u. For the authentic look sink them by `30 * scale` (at scale 0.2: `y -= 6.0`), leaving a 1.2 m ruin wall - which also matches Temple Run screen proportions.

## Exported files

Directory: `web/public/assets/obstacles/` - **23 files, 0.97 MB**. Convention: Y up, +Z = running direction, X across, **origin = centre of the track tile the obstacle ships with, y = 0 = road plane**, real APK units, raw Unity UV0 (V not flipped -> THREE `flipY = true`), area-weighted smooth normals, faces wound for three.js (CCW), no .mtl. All meshes are hollow 2.5D stage-set facades with fake-perspective apron triangles -> render **DoubleSide**, and do not trust the normals for lighting tricks.

Textures: **not copied on purpose** - both atlases are 1.6 MB each and already ship at `/assets/apk/wallTexture.png` (Temple Run Material) and `/assets/apk/treeTexture.png` (Temple Run Trees Material); the OBJs use exactly those UV atlases. The web game already loads both.

`-vert` files are the same obstacle authored for the 90-degree track section (the mesh is rotated in the prefab); use them on turn tiles if you want the exact original pairing.

**About the tree files**: each one is the complete landmark tree (190 u tall) because that is how the original ships it - the trunk is scenery that overhangs the track and the root/log (or the lean of the trunk) is the obstacle. The interaction band is the lane table: `tree-jump` blocks the centre lane 0..10 above the road, `tree-trip` 0..4, `tree-slide` is open below 11. Scale the whole tree by the same factor as the obstacle and it will read correctly (Temple Run trees are deliberately huge). Cropped variants were tried and dropped: the meshes are hollow 2.5D facades, so any Y crop exposes the fake-perspective apron slices and a chopped canopy, which looks broken in-engine.

## Recommended mapping to the web game

| game obstacle | use | files | measured basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| **hurdle** | house the low root/log at the road surface | `tree-jump-left.obj / tree-jump-right.obj`<br>`tree-trip-left.obj / tree-trip-right.obj`<br>`(+ the -vert turn variants)` | see table above |
| **arch (slide)** | the leaning tree trunk mass that clears the road below 11 u | `tree-slide.obj / tree-slide-vert.obj` | see table above |
| **block (lane change)** | a stone brazier pedestal standing in one lane | `stone-pedestal.obj   <- derived, the cleanest fit (6.2 x 14.9 x 10.1 u, SITS on the road)`<br>`narrow-wall-left/right.obj, narrow-beam-left/right.obj   (waist-high ruin walls, 1.2 m)` | see table above |
| **gap (jump)** | the stone pit rim: two ledges with a slot between them, floor below road | `pit.obj / pit-vert.obj,  pit-long-a.obj / pit-long-b.obj` | see table above |
| **fire (jump)** | the twin flame pedestals; the fire itself must stay procedural particles | `flame-tower.obj / flame-tower-vert.obj` | see table above |
| **extra stage piece** | run-through temple archway (not an obstacle you react to) | `tower-arch.obj / tower-arch-vert.obj` | see table above |

Collision: **keep it procedural.** The APK ships no obstacle hitboxes (all 286 BoxColliders are GUI/treasure triggers, e.g. the `Slider` 220x60), so the existing `main.js` collision boxes stay the source of truth; the OBJ is visual dressing attached to them.

### Scale and placement

* The APK scale is 10.8 u = the runner = 1.80 m, so **1 u ~ 0.167 m**. Do not put these into the scene at that scale - pick a factor per obstacle.
* Anchors disagree because the web game already bends proportions: player-matched scale `0.185` (10.8 u -> 2.0 game units), corridor-matched scale `0.43` (APK corridor 30 u vs the web corridor 13 u), while the web game's lane pitch is only 1.3 units. Practical recipe: scale so the obstacle's gameplay band matches the existing collision box (root top 10 u -> the ~0.85 jump height; trunk underside 11 u -> the slide window), then check with `obj-sheet.html`.
* Place with `rotation.y = 0` and the runner approaching from **-Z** (the frame is +Z = running direction). The obstacles are authored for one running direction; the left/right variants are mirrored pieces (which side the tree leans from / which lane the wall narrows).
* y = 0 is the road surface. Geometry below y = 0 (down to -35 for the trees) is the authored skirt: hide it under the road. If your road surface is a thin plane and you can see under it, offset the mesh by `-min_y * scale`.
* Origin is the **tile centre**, not the mesh XZ centre: the tree sits off to one side and the root crosses the path, which is exactly the authored alignment. Do not re-centre the tree files per-axis; use the origin.

## Does not exist in the APK

* dedicated small stone block / crate / barrel obstacle mesh (the only low meshes in the APK are the 3 coin meshes Box01/Box06/Box07, 3.6 u)
* spike trap / spikes / caltrops mesh
* broken column / rubble pile mesh
* brazier / fire pit mesh with its own flame geometry (the flame in FlameTower is a ParticleSystem, no flame mesh, no flame texture)
* statue / idol / boulder obstacle standing on the road as a lane blocker (rock_prefab, rock2, rock3 are cliff-side jungle rocks, not road props)
* separate slide-under archway mesh (the only overhead beam is the cross-beam of templeStraightTower, and the duck-under obstacle is the leaning tree of treeSlide)
* coin/pickup trap, saw blade, rotating obstacle, or any moving-obstacle mesh
* road / floor mesh with surface triangles (the endless road is procedural in the real game too)

Also checked:

* **flame mesh / fire texture**: the flame tower prefab contains `Flame Position` -> `Flame` GameObjects with 2 MonoBehaviours each, but the dump contains **0 ParticleSystem / ParticleSystemRenderer objects**; the particle settings live in IL2CPP MonoBehaviour data with no readable fields. Nothing to extract - keep the existing procedural flame/glow, just put it between the two real pedestals.
* **moving obstacles** (rotating bars, swinging blades, coin traps): none.
* **road/floor mesh**: confirmed again - the endless road is procedural in the original game too; the tiles only carry walls, never a floor surface.
* **low stone block / crate / barrel**: none. The closest real lane blocker is the flame tower pedestal, which is why `stone-pedestal.obj` is included (derived: the right-hand pedestal of `templeStraightFlameTowerHighHorz`, cut out, re-centred and dropped on y = 0; 108 v / 52 t / 6.2 x 14.9 x 10.1 u).

## Verification

Every exported OBJ was re-parsed from disk (`/tmp/verify_obstacles.py`):

* all 23 parse as OBJ with `v`/`vt`/`vn`/`f`
* vertices are finite; `len(uv) == len(v)`; `len(n) == len(v)`; every face index in range; every vertex referenced by a face
* real size and minY measured back from the file (reported in the table above)
* obstruction measured by Möller-Trumbore raycast against the *exported* geometry, per lane L(-16..-5) / C(-5..5) / R(5..16), in the road frame - this is what the table/summary above quotes, and it is how each obstacle was classified (jump / slide / gap / run-through / dodge)

Visual verification: `web/obstacle-tools/obj-sheet.html?files=...&cols=2&rows=2&view=iso` loads the exported files with the real atlases over the road plane, with a 30 x 36.8 x 60 corridor box (yellow), the 10.8 u player volume (red) and the three lane centre lines (green).

## Not exported (and why)

The remaining ~97 environment meshes are track tiles, corners, cliff-side jungle rocks (`rock*`, `rock2*`, `rock3*`), standalone trees (`treeAlone*`, `treeSlideCliff*`), ground patches (`groundPatch*`), overgrowth, the giant `templeHead` landmark, the plank-track family and the character/costume meshes. They are scenery, not obstacles; the 6 track pieces already exported by the previous pass cover the tile dressing. `Object16`/`Object21` were previously exported as "decor rock": they are in fact **the pit tile** - `pit.obj` here is the corrected reading (same mesh family, road-frame coordinates).

## Copy-paste mapping

```js
// preload (three.js importmap style used by main.js)
const obstacles = {
  hurdleL: "/assets/obstacles/tree-jump-left.obj",
  hurdleR: "/assets/obstacles/tree-jump-right.obj",
  tripL:   "/assets/obstacles/tree-trip-left.obj",
  slide:   "/assets/obstacles/tree-slide.obj",
  block:   "/assets/obstacles/stone-pedestal.obj",
  gap:     "/assets/obstacles/pit.obj",
  fire:    "/assets/obstacles/flame-tower.obj",
};
// every one of them: origin = tile centre, y = 0 = road surface, +Z = running direction,
// real APK units (1 u ~ 1/6 m), DoubleSide, tree files need alphaTest ~0.4 on treeTexture.
```
